label: input token o during the original (pre-delimiter) phase
explanation: Token detector for the letter o in the original sequence. Fires on essentially every original-phase step where the input is o (dev precision 1.00, recall 0.975), at any position 0..L-1 and for any L. Does NOT fire on o fed back during the copy phase, on the delimiter, or on other letters (rare weak activations, about 0.13-0.17 of max, on t/a in the original phase and on an o fed back at the first copy steps account for the 0.5% of mass missed). Magnitude is fairly uniform (median 0.65); in the examples, the strongest activations are an o late in a sequence that has had no earlier o, and a repeated o in the same sequence tends to activate more weakly (about 0.65-0.75 of max vs about 0.9).

issues: Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.976, mass recall 0.996, 0 false positives. Reported scores reproduce.

The missed activations are weak (about 0.13-0.15 of max) and fall into the two classes the explanation already names. (1) An o fed back at the first copy steps (recall_idx 1; 1226 dev steps, 0.2% of mass). As a predicate, phase==2 & in_tok==o & recall_idx==1 has precision 0.07, so this is sparse, not a sub-feature. (2) Original-phase a or t, often right after an o (prev_tok==o & in_tok in {a,t}: precision 0.19, recall 0.01). Neither class is big enough to justify a different predicate.

Every original-phase o fires, including a repeated o (n_seen(o)>0: precision 1.0). The claim that a repeated o is weaker is magnitude only; the examples support it (0.63 vs 0.90). The explanation already says it was not scored.
The delimiter never fires. Copy-phase activity holds 0.2% of the mass, all at recall_idx 1-2, which matches the explanation.
Minor: the profile shows firing on o at all orig_idx 0-8 at a steady rate (about 0.034 per step, about 55% of all o steps including copy-phase o). This is consistent with 'any position, any L'.
